title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-30
notes:
West leads the ♥9 against 3NT. West's lead is in response to his partner's opening bid. South should be able to come to 9 tricks via 2 spade tricks, 1 heart trick, at least 5 diamond tricks, and the ♣A. However, if the defense has a trick in diamonds, there is a danger that they will be able to take 5 tricks before South takes 9.

If a low heart is played from dummy at trick 1, East will duck. If South wins the ♥K and West has another heart and the guarded ♦K, the defense will take 4 hearts and the ♦K. If South ducks the opening lead in hand, West will switch to spades or clubs and the contract will be in trouble.

South should thus play the ♥Q from dummy at trick 1. East must win the ♥A (or South will have a second heart stopper). If East switches to a high club, South should allow him to hold the trick (or the defense might be able to take the ♥A, the ♦K, and 3 club tricks).

East will switch back to hearts. South can win the ♥K as East's opening bid showed 5 or more hearts. South crosses to the ♠K and finesses diamonds into West. West can win the ♦K, but he will be out of hearts. The ♠A and ♣A still stop the other two suits and South has 9 certain tricks.
